teaching.task: Convert composition masses to a simplest atom ratio and explain why mass ratios must become mole ratios.
teaching.causalExplanation: Atomic masses differ. Dividing each element mass by its own molar mass puts the amounts on a shared entity-count scale; normalising all mole values preserves the ratio.
teaching.conversationalApproach: Connect the known glucose/formaldehyde contrast to one worked example; explain the reason for each operation, reduce repeated instructions and let stable boards carry intermediate numbers.
teaching.openingDecision: Useful contrast: known substances can share the same simplest ratio. This earns the composition-versus-identity distinction without inventing a mystery-powder identification.
